title: Best Homemade Brownies - Love and Lemons
description: The ultimate recipe for brownies! They're fudgy, moist, and super chocolaty, with perfect crispy edges.
notes: Better chocolate chips = better brownies. Michelle Lopez recommends Ghiradelli's 60% Cacao Bittersweet Baking Chips or Enjoy Life's Dark Chocolate Morsels. It's better to pull them out too early than to leave them in too long - bake until a toothpick comes out with just a few crumbs attached. When these brownies come out of the oven, they'll be super gooey in the middle. Allow them to cool completely, about 2 hours, before you slice into them to give them a chance to set up. They'll continue to firm up the longer they're out of the oven. If you prefer a firmer brownie, store them in the fridge. Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. These also freeze well for up to a month. If you'd like to reduce the sugar, the recipe has had success with 1 cup granulated sugar instead of 1 1/2 cups. Use olive oil for a richer flavor or canola oil for a more neutral flavor. Make sure to use an 8x8 baking dish (not 9x9 or your brownies will overcook). Recipe adapted from Weeknight Baking by Michelle Lopez.

ingredients.name: cocoa powder, sifted if lumpy
ingredients.raw: 2/3 cup cocoa powder, sifted if lumpy

ingredients.name: powdered sugar, sifted if lumpy
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup powdered sugar, sifted if lumpy

ingredients.name: canola oil or extra-virgin olive oil
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup canola oil or extra-virgin olive oil

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325°F. Lightly spray an 8x8 baking dish (not a 9x9 dish or your brownies will overcook) with cooking spray and line it with parchment paper. Spray the parchment paper.
In a medium bowl, combine {i1}, {i2}, {i3}, {i4}, {i5}, and {i6}.
In a large bowl, whisk together {i7}, {i8}, {i9}, and {i10}.
Sprinkle the dry mix over the wet mix and stir until just combined.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan (it'll be thick - that's ok) and use a spatula to smooth the top.
Bake for 40 to 48 minutes, or until a toothpick comes out with only a few crumbs attached (note: it's better to pull the brownies out early than to leave them in too long).
